iconicAnchor.label: Public-service task systems with explicit steps, labels, and states
iconicAnchor.creatorOrTradition: Government Digital Service and public-sector service design
iconicAnchor.whyCanonical: The GOV.UK pattern demonstrates visible ordering, direct task labels, numbered steps, and conditional paths whose form is determined by what a person must do.

sources.title: Step by step navigation
supports: Operational information should present an end-to-end journey in logical, numbered steps ordered around user needs.
Explicit and-or branches support the guide's emphasis on visible states and action hierarchy.

sources.title: Ask users for information on a document
sources.publisher: UK Home Office User-Centred Design Manual
supports: Guidance images belong only where they help a person perform a task or locate specific information.
Images require explicit meaning and should not be added as decoration to an operational surface.

bundledReferenceRationale: Excellent single-image set. The lead clearly teaches utility signal, systematic, typographic, grid defined, retains its identity at card scale, and shows no visible anti-cue, integrity failure, or confusing overlap with neighboring styles. The independently approved lead is assets/refs/operational-utility/generated-lead.jpg. No support image is needed because the lead carries the direction without filler.
